newsitem.title: USA: FIFO accounting slashed Hess Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: FIFO accounting slashed Hess Q1 profits.

text.p: The use of first in/first out accounting left Amerada Hess Corp with minimal first quarter earnings, spokesman Carl Tursi said Monday.
The company reported first quarter net income of $4.6 million, or $0.05 per share, compared with $66 million, or $0.71 per share, a year earlier.

Citing the drop in product prices throughout the quarter, he said the impact on the company's 40 million barrels of inventory left Hess with a $56 million loss for its refining, marketing and shipping operations compared to a $44 million profit in 1996's initial quarter.
Asked about the small, $0.03 per share, earnings forecast by the First Call consensus estimate, Tursai cited the cat cracker installed last year at Hess' big Virgin Islands refinery.
As a result, "we were not clobbered as much" by the falling prices, he explained.

The company's improved exploration and production earnings of $96.6 million in the latest quarter, up from $68 million last year, and lower interest expenses of $29.3 million compared to $41.2 million did little to offset the FIFO impact. It also reported an increase in corporate expenses to $6.7 million from $4.8 million in 1996's first quarter.
Hess repoorted revenues of $2.42 billion in the first quarter of 1997 compared with $2.23 billion in 1996.

It said first quarter capital spending was $219.5 million, of which $199.5 million was related to exploration and production activities. Capital spending in the first quarter of 1996 amounted to $158.2 million, including $151.6 million for exploration and production.
"At the moment margins are very good," Tursi said, He declined to comment further after noting product margins looked pretty good when the company reported fourth quarter results in January.
